stories.title: America's new crypto bank charter isn't a full bank license
stories.summary: US regulators are creating a new charter for crypto firms, according to CryptoSlate. The charter gives firms bank-like status. It does not give them full banking rights or protections. Reporting on the exact rules is still limited.
stories.whyItMatters: The charter will shape how crypto firms hold customer funds and connect to the banking system. That affects oversight and consumer protection.
whatToWatch: Which agency finalizes the charter rules
Which crypto firms apply first
Whether deposit protections apply to charter holders
questions: What protections will customers of these "banks" actually have?
Which regulator will supervise them day to day?

sources.title: America is creating a new class of crypto banks – but they aren’t really banks

stories.title: Nigeria's proposed capital floor could cut off access to global crypto platforms
stories.summary: Nigeria is weighing a new capital floor rule for crypto platforms, per CryptoSlate. Platforms that do not meet the higher capital requirement could lose the right to serve local users. The proposal has not been finalized.
stories.whyItMatters: Nigeria has one of the largest crypto user bases in Africa. A stricter capital rule could force global platforms to exit the market.
whatToWatch: The final capital threshold set by regulators
Which platforms announce an exit or stay
Any local alternatives that fill the gap
questions: What is the proposed capital floor amount?
When would the rule take effect?

sources.title: Local’s access to global crypto platforms could end under Nigeria’s proposed capital floor

stories.title: As foreign investors dump $29B in Treasuries, Washington turns to stablecoin issuers
stories.summary: Foreign investors have sold $29 billion in Treasury bills, according to CryptoSlate. In response, Washington is reportedly looking to stablecoin issuers, which hold large Treasury reserves, as a new source of demand for US government debt.
stories.whyItMatters: This links stablecoin policy directly to US debt financing, a connection the industry views as a step toward mainstream acceptance.
whatToWatch: Any formal policy proposal on stablecoin reserve rules
Growth in stablecoin issuance tied to Treasury purchases
questions: Which issuers and mechanisms would be involved?
Does this create new risks if stablecoin demand later drops?

sources.title: As foreign investors dump $29 billion in Treasury bills, Washington pivots to stablecoin issuers to back US debt

stories.title: EU's MiCA rules set their sights on DeFi vaults
stories.summary: The EU's MiCA framework is being extended to cover DeFi vaults, per Cointelegraph. Regulators face real difficulty applying rules built for companies to decentralized, code-based products.
stories.whyItMatters: How the EU handles DeFi under MiCA will set an early template for other regions still deciding how to regulate decentralized finance.
whatToWatch: Draft guidance from EU regulators on DeFi vaults
Industry response and pushback
questions: How will regulators define a "sufficiently decentralized" vault?
Who would bear compliance liability for a DeFi product with no clear operator?

sources.title: MiCA is coming for DeFi vaults, but regulation will be difficult

stories.title: Crypto's week: bears squeezed in bitcoin and ether rally, X eyes stablecoin payouts for creators
stories.summary: CoinDesk's weekly recap covers a short squeeze that drove a rally in bitcoin and ether prices. It also reports that Elon Musk's X platform wants to pay creators in stablecoins. The roundup covers five stories from the week.
stories.whyItMatters: The squeeze shows shifting market momentum, and a stablecoin payout plan from a major platform would expand stablecoin use in everyday payments.
whatToWatch: Whether the rally holds or fades
Details on X's stablecoin payment plan, if confirmed
questions: What specifically triggered the bear squeeze?
Which stablecoin would X use, and when?

sources.title: Bitcoin and Ether bears get decimated amid 'squeeze-led' rally and Musk's X wants to pay creators in stablecoins: Crypto's week in 5 stories

stories.title: Ripple backs $275M credit line with locked XRP reserves
stories.summary: Ripple is using locked XRP reserves as collateral for a $275 million institutional credit line, according to CryptoSlate. The deal ties an institutional lending facility to the company's own token holdings.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows crypto firms increasingly using native tokens as collateral for real financial deals, linking token value to corporate credit risk.
whatToWatch: Which institutions receive the credit line
Any impact on XRP price if reserves are drawn down
questions: What happens to the credit line if XRP's price falls sharply?
Who are the lenders behind the facility?

sources.title: Ripple relies on locked XRP reserves to back a $275 million institutional credit line

stories.title: 27ms Bitcoin validation would need 17 GPU-years of compute, study finds
stories.summary: A CryptoSlate report on Bitcoin research says near-instant, 27-millisecond transaction validation would require an estimated 17 GPU-years of compute power. The figure illustrates the compute cost of pushing validation speed to that level.
stories.whyItMatters: It matters for Bitcoin scaling debates and shows the tradeoff between transaction speed and the compute resources such speed demands.
whatToWatch: Whether developers pursue this approach further
Any related protocol change proposals
questions: What hardware efficiency assumptions underlie the 17 GPU-year estimate?
Would this approach affect Bitcoin's decentralization?

sources.title: Reaching instant 27ms validation on Bitcoin will take 17 GPU years of compute power

stories.title: Second crypto boss at same firm goes missing, four years after his predecessor
stories.summary: The successor to a crypto executive who disappeared four years ago has now also gone missing, according to a New York Times report surfaced via Hacker News. Details on the firm and the circumstances are limited in current reporting.
stories.whyItMatters: A second disappearance at the same firm's leadership raises fresh questions about governance and accountability in crypto companies.
whatToWatch: Any statement from the company involved
Law enforcement involvement or investigation updates
questions: Which company and executives are involved?
Are the two disappearances connected?

sources.title: Four Years Ago, a Crypto Boss Went Missing. Now His Successor Has

stories.title: Coldcard adds 65 key-press step after seed exploit; exposed funds still need to move
stories.summary: Hardware wallet maker Coldcard now requires 65 key presses as a new security step, following a seed exploit, per CryptoSlate. Users whose funds were exposed by the flaw still need to move them to secure wallets.
stories.whyItMatters: Hardware wallets are seen as a top standard for self-custody. A seed-level exploit undermines that trust until affected users act.
whatToWatch: Coldcard guidance on migrating exposed funds
Confirmation of whether the exploit was used against real users
questions: How many wallets are actually affected?
Was the exploit used before it was disclosed?

sources.title: Coldcard now requires 65 key presses after seed exploit, while exposed funds still must move

stories.title: Grayscale's Zcash ETF filing proposes 2.5% fee and up to 34% DCG stake
stories.summary: Grayscale has filed for a Zcash ETF that proposes a 2.5% management fee, per CryptoSlate. The filing also outlines a potential stake of up to 34% for parent company DCG.
stories.whyItMatters: A Zcash ETF would be a first for a privacy-focused cryptocurrency and would test regulators' appetite for privacy coin exposure.
whatToWatch: SEC review and decision timeline
Whether other issuers file competing Zcash ETFs
questions: Will regulators treat a privacy coin ETF differently from bitcoin or ether ETFs?
What does the DCG stake mean for other investors?

sources.title: Grayscale’s Zcash ETF filing proposes a 2.5% fee and a potential 34% DCG stake

stories.title: Zcash surges 48% past $800 on Grayscale ETF news and 'next bitcoin' talk
stories.summary: Zcash jumped 48% to trade above $800, according to CoinDesk, after Grayscale's spot ETF filing. The move has fueled talk of Zcash as the "next bitcoin," a comparison that remains speculative.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows how a single ETF filing can rapidly move the price of a smaller-cap token, a useful signal for gauging real risk versus hype.
whatToWatch: Whether the price gain holds as the ETF review process plays out
Any regulatory response to the rally
questions: How much of the move reflects fundamentals rather than speculation?

sources.title: Zcash jumps 48% to over $800 as Grayscale spot ETF push adds to ‘next bitcoin’ buzz

stories.title: New Illinois rules could hit crypto users with monthly tax bills on total asset value
stories.summary: New Illinois rules could produce monthly tax bills based on the total value of a person's crypto holdings, if covered brokers fail to collect the tax themselves, per CryptoSlate. The rule could affect everyday holders, not only active traders.
stories.whyItMatters: A state rule that taxes total holdings, rather than realized gains, would be a notable departure from typical federal tax treatment.
whatToWatch: Final implementation of the rule
How brokers adjust to the collection requirement
Any legal challenges to the rule
questions: Does the rule tax unrealized value, or only cover missed withholding?
Which brokers count as "covered" under the rule?

sources.title: Everyday crypto users face monthly tax bills on total asset value if covered brokers fail to collect under new Illinois rules
